hubspot.1: In HubSpot, open Settings › Integrations › Private Apps (in newer accounts: Development › Legacy apps) and create a private app.
hubspot.2: Name it (for example, zerosoft import). In Scopes, add the read scopes listed below. Nothing is written to HubSpot.
hubspot.3: Create the app and copy its access token (it starts with pat-).
hubspot.4: Paste it below and connect. We check the token and show what will come in: counts, owners, pipelines and custom properties.
hubspot.5: Map each HubSpot owner to a person in the workspace (they match by email) or invite the ones who are missing, then start.

pipedrive.1: In Pipedrive, open your avatar › Personal preferences › API.
pipedrive.2: Copy your personal API token. Use an admin account so the records of everyone come in.
pipedrive.3: Paste it below, review the preview and start.

notionApi.1: Open notion.so/profile/integrations and create a new internal integration for your workspace.
notionApi.2: In Capabilities, keep Read content on and turn on Read user information including email addresses, so people match workspace members. It doesn’t need insert or update.
notionApi.3: Copy the Internal Integration Secret (it starts with ntn_ or secret_).
notionApi.4: In Notion, on each top level page you want to bring: ••• › Connections › add your integration. Its subpages and databases come with it.
notionApi.5: Paste the secret below, choose where the pages go, review the counts and start.

notionZip.1: In Notion, open Settings › General › Export all workspace content (or ••• › Export on a single page).
notionZip.2: Choose Markdown & CSV, include subpages and files, and download the .zip.
notionZip.3: Upload the .zip below. Large exports are uploaded in parts.

confluence.1: In Confluence, open Space settings › Export space and choose HTML.
confluence.2: Download the .zip and upload it below.

gdocs.1: In Google Drive, select the documents (or a folder) and download them: Drive zips them as .docx.
gdocs.2: Upload the .zip or the .docx files below.

linear.1: In Linear, open Settings › Account › Security & access › Personal API keys and create a new key.
linear.2: Give it Read access (nothing is written to Linear) and copy it.
linear.3: Paste it below and pick the target project.

jira.1: Open id.atlassian.com › Security › API tokens and create an API token.
jira.2: Copy it. You also need the email of that Atlassian account and your site address (https://acme.atlassian.net).
jira.3: Paste them below with a project key (ENG) or a JQL query.

github.1: In GitHub, open Settings › Developer settings › Personal access tokens › Fine-grained tokens and generate a new token.
github.2: Give it access to the repository and the read-only permissions listed below.
github.3: Paste it below with the repository as owner/repo.

asana.1: In Asana, open your profile › Settings › Apps › Developer console and create a personal access token.
asana.2: Paste it below with the project URL.

shortcut.1: In Shortcut, open Settings › API Tokens and generate a token.
shortcut.2: Paste it below. Leave the search empty to bring every story that is not archived.

trackCsv.1: Export your issues as CSV from your tool (Linear and Jira have presets).
trackCsv.2: Upload the file below and map its columns.

calendly.1: In Calendly, open Integrations & apps › API and webhooks.
calendly.2: Under Personal access tokens, generate a token and copy it.
calendly.3: Paste it below. Upcoming bookings are optional.

bitly.1: In Bitly, open Settings › API and generate an access token.
bitly.2: Open the Link importer and paste it there.

evernote.1: In Evernote, export a notebook as .enex (right click the notebook › Export notebook).
evernote.2: In Notes, use Import in the sidebar and choose the .enex file.

appsPanel.desc: Turn each app on or off for the workspace, choose who gets it (everyone, teams or people) and override it per person. Turning one off removes it everywhere for everyone; what's inside is kept.
